jobs.title: Program Manager, Third Party Risk
jobs.description:
Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About The Team

The Third Party Risk Management (TPRM) team is accountable for defining, maintaining, and overseeing the third-party risk framework, policy, and inventory in accordance with management expectations and best practices. We are focused on assessing and managing risks exposed through our relationships with third parties, adhering to regulatory guidance, and driving operational efficiencies across risk teams.

What you'll do

In this role, you'll support and maintain a robust framework for identifying, assessing, and managing third-party risks to protect Stripe. You'll partner with cross-functional Risk Domain Owners, Procurement subteams, Legal, and other stakeholders to apply a unified Third Party Risk Framework across risk and compliance areas. You'll maintain the existing Stripe Third Party Risk Program, Policy, and Standards, while further developing new Standards to propel the maturity of the Third Party Risk Program.

Responsibilities

Maintain the Global Third Party Risk Management Program, Policy, and Framework, ensuring alignment with relevant regulations, standards, and best practices
Launch and mature nascent risk domains to increase overall program maturity
Design and support an enhanced oversight model for specialized third-party types including Partnerships and Contingent Workers
Design and enhance elements of the existing Third Party Risk Framework including offboarding and incident monitoring, among other areas
Build and oversee the third-party performance management function and define performance standards, including metric templates and ongoing monitoring activities, to ensure third-party health
Design effective reporting to monitor and communicate the third-party risk program status, key issues, and remediation plans to governance committees, senior leaders, and relevant stakeholders
Serve as subject matter expert and coordinator of system business requirements among risk domain owners and stakeholders—prioritizing effective requirements (Users First and Risk Focused)

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum Requirements

4+ years of experience in risk or compliance roles, preferably third-party risk in a regulated environment
Proven experience managing distinct projects and programs, with particularly strong skills in stakeholder management
Strong written and verbal communication skills—including the ability to communicate effectively with different stakeholders across the business such as risk domain owners, internal audit, and the broader risk and compliance community
Excellent cross-functional collaboration skills, including navigating leadership and interpersonal working relationships
Strong organizational and time management skills
Ability to handle multiple assignments while comfortably managing ambiguity
Ability to assess and analyze data in order to solve problems and draw insightful conclusions

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience building third-party risk programs
Previous experience implementing programs around regulatory frameworks
Understanding of risk program elements including policy and risk appetite creation and maintenance
Understanding of risk areas such as information security, privacy, business continuity, finance, reputation, operational, and ESG
Experience with Tableau or other data visualization tools

In-office expectations

Office-assigned Stripes in most of our locations are currently expected to spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This expectation may vary depending on role, team and location. For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible.

Pay and benefits

The annual US base salary range for this role is $123,600 - $185,400. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the US may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process.

Additional benefits for this role may include: equity, company bonus or sales commissions/bonuses; 401(k) plan; medical, dental, and vision benefits; and wellness stipends.

We look forward to hearing from you.

At Stripe, we're looking for people with passion, grit, and integrity. You're encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't precisely match the job description. Your skills and passion will stand out—and set you apart—especially if your career has taken some extraordinary twists and turns. At Stripe, we welcome diverse perspectives and people who think rigorously and aren't afraid to challenge assumptions. Join us.

Apply now

COMSEC Security Program Analyst

The Opportunity:

Provide technical and financial analytic support to the client’s Communications Security (COMSEC), Cryptographic, and Cybersecurity programs and efforts to ensure requirements align with Navy, Joint, and DoD strategic COMSEC and cybersecurity goals and objectives. Conduct research and analysis on COMSEC, cryptography, cybersecurity, and IT network technical and financial requirements, budgets, and policy compliance to support the development of information papers and briefings for senior client leadership. Actively participate in the planning and support of DoD COMSEC, network, and cybersecurity meetings to assess policy, requirements, and warfare capabilities to ensure the client’s positions are accurately presented. Create analytic products to support all phases of the Planning, Programming, Budgeting, and Execution (PPBE) cycle, including Program Objective Memorandum (POM) development, integration of COMSEC and technical requirements, and efforts to track developing strategies. Provide programmatic analysis and assessments of information assurance and cybersecurity requirements and capabilities to support and defend the client’s strategic investments.

You Have:

Experience with COMSEC, Cryptographic, Encryption, or Cybersecurity operations for Navy and DoD programs
Knowledge of PPBE and requirements generation processes
Knowledge of Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, PowerPoint, and Excel
Ability to leverage technical, analytic, and communication to develop and brief material to senior client leadership to support decision-making
TS/SCI clearance
Bachelor's degree and 7+ years of experience in COMSEC, IT, Command, Control, Communication, Computers, Intelligence, Surveillance, Reconnaissance (C4ISR), Space, or Unmanned Systems, or 10+ years of experience in COMSEC, IT, C4ISR, Space, or Unmanned Systems in lieu of a degree

Nice If You Have:

Experience with Navy staff as military, civilian, or contractor in OPNAV or Navy Systems Commands (SYSCOMs)
Experience with Navy Financial Management or IT systems and databases
Knowledge of Navy cryptographic systems or devices currently in service and under development
Ability to work independently, collaboratively, creatively, and analytically in a problem-solving environment
Possession of excellent verbal and written communication skills
Possession of excellent organizational skills

Clearance:

At Booz Allen, we celebrate your contributions, provide you with opportunities and choices, and support your total well-being. Contribute to projects to enhance and optimize due diligence strategy systems and tools

Experience analyzing feedback patterns and using those insights to drive process and tooling improvements

new_jobs.title: Project Manager
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

The Axel Group is currently seeking a Project Manager to join our client’s team in the Orlando, FL area. Our client partners with leading contractors and builders across the commercial, institutional, healthcare, and industrial sectors, providing everything from tools and safety products to custom-fabricated strut grids, pipe hangers, and pre-engineered support systems. With a strong reputation, national footprint, and long-standing relationships throughout the construction industry, the company continues to grow its presence in key markets including healthcare, data centers, infrastructure, and commercial development.

The Project Manager role is a hands-on, high-ownership position focused on managing projects from award through installation and contract closeout. This individual will work closely with general contractors, construction managers, field crews, vendors, customers, and internal leadership to coordinate project requirements, maintain schedules, address issues, and ensure work is completed successfully. The role offers significant autonomy and the opportunity to take ownership of multiple projects while serving as a key point of contact throughout the project lifecycle.

While the position is primarily focused on Project Management, there is also a light estimating and preconstruction component. This includes reviewing drawings and specifications, assisting with material takeoffs, gathering pricing, reviewing project scopes, and supporting estimates and change orders. The ideal candidate does not need to be a career estimator, but should be comfortable reading construction documents, understanding project scope, and working with both field and office teams.

This position offers the opportunity to join a stable, privately held organization with 40+ years of industry experience, a national footprint, and significant resources behind its continued growth. You’ll work on a diverse range of projects while building relationships with some of the industry’s leading contractors and construction professionals. The company provides a competitive compensation package, full benefits including medical, dental, vision, PTO, and 401(k), along with strong opportunities for professional development and long-term career advancement.

Job Duties & Responsibilities

Manage multiple construction projects from initial kickoff through installation and final contract closeout.
Take ownership of project execution, ensuring work progresses according to plans, specifications, schedules, budgets, and contractual requirements.
Coordinate project schedules, materials, field installation crews, contractors, vendors, customers, and internal teams.
Serve as a primary point of contact for customers, general contractors, construction managers, and other project stakeholders throughout the project lifecycle.
Review construction drawings, specifications, submittals, and contract documents to understand project scope and requirements.
Coordinate with field teams and installation crews to ensure projects are properly executed and completed in accordance with project requirements and quality standards.
Monitor project progress, materials, costs, schedules, and overall execution while proactively identifying potential issues.
Troubleshoot project challenges and work with internal and external teams to resolve issues that may impact schedule, cost, quality, or customer satisfaction.
Maintain regular communication with customers, contractors, vendors, and internal leadership regarding project status, priorities, and next steps.
Assist with light estimating, material takeoffs, pricing, and proposal development for new and existing project opportunities.
Review project scopes and assist with obtaining material, fabrication, and subcontractor pricing as needed.
Support the preparation and management of change orders, project documentation, billings, and contract closeout.
Coordinate with the sales team and internal leadership on new opportunities and ongoing customer relationships.
Visit active jobsites throughout the assigned regional territory to support project execution, customer needs, and field teams.
Maintain organized project records and ensure required documentation is accurate and submitted in a timely manner.
Work independently while managing multiple projects and priorities across different stages of construction.

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Strong understanding of construction processes and project management principles.
Ability to read, interpret, and work from construction drawings, specifications, and contract documents.
Ability to understand project scope and identify material, labor, and installation requirements.
Basic estimating and quantity takeoff experience preferred; this is a Project Management-focused position with a light estimating component.
Strong organizational and time-management skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
Excellent communication and relationship-building skills when working with customers, contractors, field teams, vendors, and internal personnel.
Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to anticipate issues and take ownership of finding solutions.
Comfortable working in both office and field environments and regularly visiting active construction sites.
Ability to work independently and make decisions while keeping customers and internal leadership informed.
Strong attention to detail, follow-through, and sense of urgency.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and general project management software; familiarity with AutoCAD, BIM, or construction-related software is a plus.

Education & Experience Requirements

3+ years of experience in construction project management, project coordination, or a related construction role preferred.
Construction-related degree or technical education preferred, but equivalent industry experience will be considered.
Experience managing projects from kickoff through installation and closeout is highly preferred.
Experience working with general contractors, construction managers, subcontractors, vendors, or field installation teams preferred.
Ability to read and interpret construction plans, specifications, and project documentation.
Previous estimating, takeoff, or preconstruction experience is a plus but not the primary focus of the position.
Ability and willingness to travel throughout the assigned regional territory to support active projects and customers.
Valid driver's license and ability to travel between project locations as needed.

Compensation & Benefits

Our client offers a competitive compensation package along with a strong benefits program, including:
Car allowance
Performance-based incentive opportunities
Medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) with company match
Paid time off and company holidays
Ongoing training and professional development
Career advancement opportunities
Long-term career stability with an established organization

Why Join Our Client

Join a privately held organization with 40+ years of proven success and a strong reputation within the construction industry.
Be part of a company with a national footprint and $600M+ in annual revenue, providing the resources and stability of a large organization while maintaining a strong, relationship-driven culture.
Work alongside a team with long-standing relationships with leading contractors, builders, and construction professionals across the country.
Gain exposure to projects across healthcare, data centers, infrastructure upgrades, commercial development, and other major construction markets.
Take meaningful ownership of projects from initial kickoff through installation and final closeout rather than being limited to one portion of the project lifecycle.
Build relationships directly with customers, contractors, construction managers, vendors, and field teams.
Join a role that combines project management, customer interaction, field coordination, problem-solving, and light estimating.
Work in a position offering significant autonomy and the ability to make an impact on day-to-day project execution.
Join an organization experiencing continued growth with opportunities to take on additional responsibility and advance your career over the long term.

. A significant part of your work will involve identifying, developing, and negotiating partnerships with venues and external stakeholders, while collaborating cross-functionally with departments such as Marketing, Operations, and Finance to bring experiences to life.

About the Role:

The role combines project management, commercial development, and strategic partnerships, with a strong emphasis on venue negotiations, relationship management, and networking within the local entertainment and events ecosystem.

About Rethink

Rethink Electric is a leading commercial and industrial solar electrical contractor with more than 15 years of experience and more than 1,000 projects installed. We specialize in the construction and installation of commercial and industrial solar projects across the United States, including rooftop and ground-mount systems.

Rethink partners with solar developers, EPCs, building owners and other project stakeholders to safely and efficiently construct high-quality solar energy systems.

Position Overview

Rethink Electric is seeking an experienced Project Manager – Solar EPC Construction to lead the execution and delivery of commercial and industrial solar projects throughout the United States.
This is a construction-focused EPC Project Manager position, not an owner/developer project management role. The Project Manager will be responsible for managing projects from Notice to Proceed (NTP) and mobilization through construction, commissioning, Substantial Completion and final turnover to the customer/O&M team.

The Project Manager will serve as the primary point of coordination between Rethink's field operations, engineering, procurement, subcontractors, customers and other project stakeholders. The successful candidate will be accountable for delivering projects safely, on schedule, within budget, in accordance with contract requirements, and to Rethink's quality standards.
The ideal candidate is a hands-on construction project manager who understands how solar projects are actually built and can effectively manage the people, materials, schedule, costs, contracts and issues required to successfully execute a project.

Key Responsibilities

Project Execution & Construction Management

Lead the execution of commercial and industrial rooftop and ground-mount solar projects from NTP through final completion.
Develop and maintain project execution plans and coordinate project mobilization.
Establish clear project objectives, responsibilities, milestones and deliverables for internal teams and subcontractors.
Coordinate engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning activities to ensure successful project execution.
Work closely with the Superintendent, Foremen and field crews to identify and resolve construction issues.
Monitor daily and weekly construction progress and take corrective action when performance does not meet the project plan.
Develop and implement recovery plans when projects fall behind schedule.
Ensure construction activities are performed in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, contract requirements and applicable codes.

Schedule Management

Develop, maintain and actively manage the project baseline schedule.
Establish and manage critical path activities and contractual milestones.
Develop and maintain three-week and other short-term look-ahead schedules as required.
Track project progress against planned production and milestone dates.
Identify schedule risks and develop mitigation and recovery strategies.
Coordinate schedule impacts associated with engineering, permitting, procurement, material deliveries, weather, subcontractors and customer requirements.
Communicate schedule status and potential delays to project leadership and customers in a timely manner.

Subcontractor & Field Team Management

Manage and coordinate subcontractors throughout project execution.
Establish clear expectations for schedule, production, quality, safety, documentation and contract compliance.
Monitor subcontractor performance and address deficiencies promptly.
Review subcontractor schedules, manpower levels and productivity.
Coordinate with field leadership to ensure adequate manpower, equipment and materials are available to maintain the project schedule.
Support subcontractor procurement, scope alignment, negotiations and performance management.

Procurement & Material Management

Coordinate project procurement activities with the estimating, procurement and operations teams.
Track major equipment and material procurement from purchase through delivery to the project site.
Identify long-lead items and material risks that could impact the construction schedule.
Coordinate material deliveries, site logistics and equipment requirements.
Resolve material shortages, damaged materials, incorrect deliveries and other procurement issues that affect project execution.

Cost & Financial Management

Manage project budgets and monitor actual and committed costs against the approved project budget.
Maintain accurate project cost forecasts and identify potential cost exposures.
Review subcontractor invoices, purchase orders and project expenditures.
Identify cost impacts associated with changes, delays, productivity issues and unforeseen conditions.
Work with project leadership to develop and implement cost-control measures.
Support monthly project forecasting and financial reporting.

Contract & Change Management

Manage project execution in accordance with the EPC contract, subcontract agreements, drawings, specifications and other contractual requirements.
Identify changes in scope and document potential cost and schedule impacts.
Prepare and support change order requests, claims and other contractual correspondence.
Ensure required notices are issued in accordance with contractual requirements.
Maintain appropriate documentation to protect Rethink's contractual position.
Monitor subcontractor compliance with contractual obligations.

Customer & Stakeholder Management

Serve as a primary point of contact for the customer during construction.
Lead or participate in weekly construction and project status meetings.
Provide accurate project status updates, including schedule, cost, progress, risks, issues and recovery actions.
Maintain professional relationships with customers, subcontractors, consultants, utilities, AHJs and other project stakeholders.

Quality, Safety & Compliance

Support Rethink's safety culture and ensure project activities are performed in accordance with company safety requirements and project-specific requirements.
Coordinate quality control activities and ensure work complies with approved plans, specifications and applicable codes.

Commissioning, Completion & Turnover

Coordinate construction completion activities with commissioning and operations teams.
Support system energization, testing and commissioning activities.
Manage punch-list development and completion. .

Project Documentation & Reporting

Maintain accurate project records within Procore and other company systems.
Manage RFIs, submittals, meeting minutes, daily reports, schedules, change documentation and other project records.
Prepare weekly and monthly project reports.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Business, Architecture or a related field preferred; equivalent construction experience will be considered.
5+ years of construction project management experience, preferably with commercial/industrial electrical, renewable energy or solar EPC projects.
Demonstrated experience managing construction projects from mobilization through completion and turnover.
Commercial or industrial solar construction experience strongly preferred.
Experience managing subcontractors and field construction teams.
Strong understanding of construction scheduling, project controls, procurement and cost management.
Experience with contract administration, change orders and subcontractor management.
Proficiency with Procore, Microsoft Project, Primavera P6 or similar construction/project management software.
Strong Excel skills and the ability to analyze project cost and schedule information.
Ability to read and understand construction drawings, specifications, contracts and project schedules.
Strong written and verbal communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities and projects in a fast-paced construction environment.
Willingness to travel to project sites as required.
Strong problem-solving skills with a proactive approach to identifying and resolving project issues.

Full-time position with competitive compensation commensurate with experience.

Discretionary bonus opportunities.
401(k) employer match.
Health, vision and dental benefits.
Paid time off, including company holidays.
Opportunity for advancement within a growing renewable energy construction company.

Amentum is seeking an experienced Project Manager
(SME) to support Combatant Command Operations in the Information Environment (OIE) under the Apollo program. The Apollo Solutions Architect Team (ASAT) is a cross-functional enterprise team that drives innovation, standardization, and integration across all Apollo Task Order services. ASAT serves as Apollo’s dedicated SME cell, delivering scalable support to Combatant Commands through advanced solution design, operational integration, training, analysis, and modernization. Centrally based in Tampa, the ASAT continuously develops and deploys new tools, workflows, and TTPs to outpace adversaries and strengthen Combatant Command information advantage.

As a member of ASAT, the selected candidate will manage integrated capability-development projects that improve how Apollo plans, fields, adopts, sustains, and assesses OIE/IW capabilities across Combatant Commands and mission partners. This role applies a holistic capability-lines-of-development approach — including doctrine/TTPs, organization, training, materiel/tools, leadership, personnel, facilities, policy, and process integration — to ensure new capabilities are operationally relevant, adoptable, measurable, scalable, and aligned with Government objectives. The Project Manager (SME) will coordinate cross-functional teams, manage Integrated Project Plans, track risks and dependencies, synchronize stakeholder inputs, and drive implementation of enterprise solutions that improve planning, operations, assessment, mission-enabling services, and decision support.

As a Project Manager (SME), you will:

Serve as a senior member of the Apollo Solution Architect Team (ASAT), supporting enterprise-level capability development, modernization, and integration across all Apollo Task Order services.
Manage cross-functional capability-development projects using a holistic lines-of-development approach that considers doctrine/TTPs, organization, training, materiel/tools, leadership, personnel, facilities, policy, processes, data, and sustainment requirements.
Lead development, coordination, execution, and update of Integrated Project Plans (IPPs), including project objectives, milestones, staffing/resource requirements, risks, dependencies, deliverables, implementation schedules, and ROI considerations.
Translate Combatant Command and mission-partner operational needs into executable project plans, implementation roadmaps, decision-support products, and capability-integration strategies.
Coordinate across ASAT Solutions Managers, Solutions Designers, Innovation SMEs, Plans/Ops SMEs, Assessment SMEs, Data/AI SMEs, Knowledge Managers, Training/Adoption SMEs, and operational stakeholders to ensure capability solutions are fully integrated and operationally executable.
Support capability gap analysis, requirements decomposition, stakeholder analysis, implementation planning, and sustainment planning for OIE/IW tools, workflows, data architectures, assessment methods, planning processes, and operational support capabilities.
Ensure new or improved capabilities are aligned with Apollo objectives, Task Order requirements, CCMD campaign priorities, joint planning processes, and Government-directed operational timelines.
Develop project management artifacts, including project charters, implementation plans, milestone schedules, risk registers, decision logs, action trackers, project briefs, capability roadmaps, and executive-level status updates.
Identify risks, interdependencies, constraints, and mitigation actions affecting capability implementation, including security, classification, data-access, staffing, stakeholder coordination, technical integration, adoption, training, and sustainment considerations.
Support change management and capability adoption by ensuring users, staffs, planners, analysts, and leadership understand how new tools, workflows, processes, and methodologies improve mission execution.
Coordinate pilot efforts, proof-of-concept activities, capability demonstrations, user-feedback sessions, after-action reviews, and continuous-improvement cycles.
Develop measures of performance, measures of effectiveness, adoption metrics, utilization indicators, and ROI inputs to assess capability value and inform prioritization decisions.
Support integration of advanced technologies, digital tools, data-management approaches, AI-enabled analytics, collaboration platforms, and knowledge-management solutions into operational workflows.
Maintain alignment between project execution, ASAT innovation priorities, PMO governance, CCMD requirements, task-level deliverables, and Apollo’s enterprise operating model.
Prepare and deliver executive-level briefings, project status updates, recommendations, decision papers, implementation plans, and lessons-learned products for Government and Amentum leadership.
Travel CONUS/OCONUS as required to support capability implementation, stakeholder engagement, project coordination, training/adoption support, and mission-partner requirements.

Required Qualifications

Must have an active Secret security clearance.
Bachelor’s degree in Project Management, Program Management, Business Administration, National Security Studies, Military Studies, Information Operations, Operations Research, Organizational Development, Systems Engineering, Data Analytics, Public Administration, or a related discipline.
Minimum 11 years of experience supporting project management, program management, capability development, capability integration, operational planning, mission support, transformation, modernization, or related national-security mission areas.
Demonstrated experience managing complex projects involving multiple stakeholders, technical contributors, operational users, dependencies, risks, schedules, and deliverables.
Experience supporting military operations, Combatant Commands, Joint organizations, government mission environments, or complex DoD programs.
Strong understanding of OIE, Information Advantage, Information Forces integration, operational intelligence, campaign planning, assessment, knowledge management, digital modernization, and Joint operational environments.
Experience developing project plans, implementation roadmaps, risk registers, action trackers, decision logs, project schedules, executive briefings, or capability-development documentation.
Demonstrated ability to translate operational requirements into executable project plans, capability-integration strategies, and measurable implementation outcomes.
Experience coordinating cross-functional teams that may include planners, analysts, technologists, data specialists, training/adoption personnel, operations SMEs, assessment personnel, and leadership stakeholders.
Ability to assess capability gaps, define implementation requirements, manage dependencies, identify risk, and recommend practical mitigation actions.
Strong written, verbal, facilitation, coordination, and executive briefing skills.
Ability to operate in fast-paced, ambiguous, multi-stakeholder environments while maintaining schedule discipline, traceability, accountability, and mission focus.

Active Top Secret security clearance and SCI eligibility. U.S. Citizenship is required to obtain a Top Secret clearance.
Master’s degree in Project Management, Program Management, National Security Studies, Strategic Studies, Military Studies, Organizational Development, Systems Engineering, Data Analytics, Operations Research, or a related field.

Prior experience as a Project Manager, Program Manager, Capability Development Lead, Capability Integration Manager, Operations Integrator, Mission Integration Lead, PMO Lead, or equivalent role supporting complex government or defense programs.
Experience managing projects that integrate multiple capability lines of development, including doctrine/TTPs, organization, training, materiel/tools, leadership, personnel, facilities, policy, process, data, and sustainment considerations.
Experience supporting OIE, IW, PSYOP, Cyber, STO, JEMSO, DDA, OPSEC, Public Affairs, Civil-Military Operations, Assessment, Data Analytics, Operational Intelligence, Knowledge Management, or related mission areas.

new_jobs.title: Business Analyst – FEC Screening Systems (Sanction Detection)
new_jobs.description:
Bedrijfsomschrijving

Sopra Steria biedt op maat gemaakte end-to-end corporate technology en software solutions aan die organisaties helpen gedurfde keuzes te maken en resultaten te boeken. En met succes! Met meer dan 51.000 collega’s in bijna 30 landen behoren we tot de top van de Europese digital solutions leveranciers. Succesvolle organisaties in Europa vertrouwen op onze technologie omdat we blijven streven naar innovatie, samenwerking en zakelijke ontwikkeling.

The world is how we shape it.

Let’s shape it together.

Vacatureomschrijving

Stap in de cruciale wereld van Know Your Customer (KYC) en het bestrijden van financiële criminaliteit (FEC) bij banken en financiële instellingen. Sopra Steria staat aan de frontlinie van het beschermen van het financiële systeem met geavanceerde, data-gedreven Sanction Screening-technologieën. Dit proces detecteert transacties waarbij personen of organisaties betrokken zijn die mogelijk risico’s vormen op het gebied van sancties, terrorismefinanciering of witwassen.

Wat ga je doen?

Als Business Analyst speel je een sleutelrol in het vormgeven, testen en afstemmen van onze sanctie screening systemen en -modellen op het beleid, de risicostandaarden en compliance procedures van de klant. Je bent verantwoordelijk voor de volledige levenscyclus van jouw features – van het definiëren van de requirements en begeleiden van de implementatie tot het monitoren van de prestaties en rapporteren van de resultaten. Je bent zowel een strategische denker als een hands-on analist, in staat om complexe zakelijke behoeften te vertalen naar duidelijke en uitvoerbare taken voor jouw squad.

Jouw verantwoordelijkheden/taken zijn:

Specificeren van zakelijke en technische vereisten via interviews, workshops, demo’s en samenwerking
Definiëren van duidelijke en testbare acceptatiecriteria voor features en epics
Prioriteren en onderscheid maken tussen wereldwijde ‘must-haves’ en ‘nice-to-haves’ om de integriteit van wereldwijde standaarden te waarborgen
Analyseren en beoordelen van sanctie screening algoritmen, regels en drempels, en verbeteringen aanbevelen
Nauw samenwerken met Product Owners om backlog refinement en squadprioriteiten af te stemmen
Technische concepten en oplossingen helder communiceren naar internationale stakeholders
Zorgen dat alle oplossingen voldoen aan interne beleidslijnen, standaarden en regelgeving
Uitvoeren van data-analyse en mapping; oplossingen voorstellen voor datakwaliteitsproblemen
Stimuleren van een feedbackcultuur en een proactieve, oplossingsgerichte houding onderhouden

Functie-eisen

Wij zijn op zoek naar gepassioneerde collega’s die graag de grenzen verleggen op het gebied van digitale transformatie en technologieconsultancy. Bij Sopra Steria krijg je de kans om je vaardigheden verder te ontwikkelen in een constructieve, samenwerkende teamomgeving, waarbij je werkt aan impactvolle projecten die verandering teweegbrengen voor onze klanten. Als je gedijt op uitdagingen en (de meeste van) de onderstaande kwalificaties bezit, kijken we uit naar je sollicitatie!

Type dienstverband: Hybride

Locatie: Nieuwegein

Aantal uren: 32-40 uur werkweek

Contractduur: Eén jaar, met uitzicht op een vast dienstverband

Opleiding: Je hebt een afgeronde hbo- of wo-opleiding afgerond

Talen: Nederlands (vereist)

We zoeken iemand met de volgende vaardigheden:

Minimaal 2,5 jaar relevante werkervaring als business analyst, bij voorkeur in de financiële sector
Ervaring met Sanction Screening of bredere FEC-domeinen is zeer gewenst (maar geen must)
Bekendheid met risico- en compliance-architectuur, inclusief tools zoals Inform RiskShield, Python, Databricks
Affiniteit met data analyse: in staat om data lineage analyses, kwaliteitsbeoordelingen en privacy reviews uit te voeren
Ervaring met modeltesten, risicostandaarden en rapportages aan toezichthouders
Vaardigheid om samen te werken met diverse stakeholders zoals Compliance, IT en Business Operations
Sterk functioneel inzicht in enterprise IT-landschappen
Ervaring met Agile, Scrum, DevOps, Lean of SAFe methodologieën

Daarnaast breng je de volgende persoonlijke vaardigheden mee:

Sterk analytisch denkvermogen en probleemoplossend vermogen
In staat om zowel strategisch als gedetailleerd te werken
Uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden, met het vermogen om technische en niet-technische stakeholders te betrekken
Hoog niveau van documentatie- en rapportagevaardigheden – nauwkeurig, onderbouwd en audit-ready
Zelfstandig en georganiseerd, met het vermogen om meerdere initiatieven tegelijk te managen

Aanvullende informatie

Je zal deel uitmaken van een grote naam in de tech wereld die bekend is om consulting, digitale diensten en softwareontwikkeling. Je begeeft je tussen high-level professionals die durven in te zetten om hoge resultaten te behalen. Daarnaast maak je ook deel uit van onze Data area.

Bij Sopra Steria – Financial Economic Crime (FEC) voorzien we banken en financiële instellingen van digitale tools om risico’s te beheren, klanten te beschermen en de impact van financiële economische criminaliteit te beperken. Als poortwachters van het financiële systeem spelen banken een cruciale rol in de bescherming van onze economie tegen criminele inmenging. Daardoor worden financiële instellingen onderworpen aan steeds strengere regelgeving en toezicht. Tegelijkertijd maken wereldwijde economische instabiliteit en steeds geavanceerdere, technologiegedreven financiële criminaliteit het werk van banken steeds moeilijker.

Enkele cijfers: Naar schatting wordt jaarlijks 16 miljard euro aan crimineel geld witgewassen in Nederland. Minder dan 1% van de criminele geldstromen die via het mondiale banksysteem gaan, wordt daadwerkelijk gestopt. Daarom moeten banken hun aanpak radicaal veranderen in de strijd tegen FEC. Gelukkig zijn er tactische veranderingen die banken snel kunnen doorvoeren om het effect van financiële economische criminaliteit te verminderen.

Bij Sopra Steria zorgen we ervoor dat jij je werk met plezier én in balans kunt doen. Daarom bieden we een aantrekkelijk en flexibel pakket aan arbeidsvoorwaarden:

Een vast contract en een salaris tussen de €3.000,- en €6.000,- bruto per maand (op basis van 40 uur per week). De exacte inschaling hangt af van jouw ervaring en de rol;
Vakantiegeld van 8%;
Sociale activiteiten met collega’s, van gezellige borrels tot sportieve of inhoudelijke uitjes;
Ontwikkelmogelijkheden via trainingen, kennisdelingssessies en inspirerende (netwerk)events;
Hybride werken: thuis of op kantoor, afhankelijk van wat jij nodig hebt;
Een royaal mobiliteitsbudget, in de vorm van een leaseregeling van €892,- met de keuze uit een elektrische leaseauto met NS Business Card of leasefiets of een alternatief vervoersregeling van €1.007,- net wat het beste bij jouw manier van reizen past;
Winstdeling van 8% on target;
27 betaalde vakantiedagen
Mogelijkheid om op fiscaal vriendelijke manier studieschuld af te lossen, een fiets, zonnepanelen of sportabonnementen aan te schaffen (Cafetaria-systeem) of andere personeelskortingen te verkrijgen;
Een internetvergoeding en thuiswerkvergoeding waarbij wij jou faciliteiten bieden voor de uitrusting van jouw eigen thuiskantoor;
Een flexibele pensioenregeling, waaraan jij, op maat en passend bij jou, bijdragen kunt toevoegen.

______

Sopra Steria is een werkgever die gelijke kansen biedt. Alle gekwalificeerde sollicitanten worden in aanmerking genomen voor een job zonder rekening te houden met leeftijd, afkomst, nationaliteit, huidskleur, verlof voor familie- of medische zorg, geslachtsidentiteit of -uitdrukking, genetische informatie, immigratiestatus, burgerlijke staat, medische toestand, nationale herkomst, fysieke of mentale handicap, politieke voorkeur, beschermde veteranen- of militaire status, ras, etniciteit, religie, geslacht (inclusief zwangerschap), seksuele geaardheid of enig ander kenmerk dat wordt beschermd door toepasselijke lokale wetten, voorschriften en verordeningen. We koesteren een werkomgeving die inclusief is en alle verschillen respecteert.

The Center for International Private Enterprise (CIPE) strengthens democracy around the world through private enterprise and market-oriented reform. CIPE is one of the four core institutes of the National Endowment for Democracy and is an affiliate of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce. Since 1983, CIPE has worked with business leaders, policymakers, and civil society to build the institutions vital to a democratic society. CIPE’s key program areas include Enterprise Ecosystems, Democratic Governance, Business Advocacy, Women’s Economic Empowerment, Anti-Corruption & Ethics, and Trade.

Position:
Senior Program Manager
Reports to:
Regional Hub Director, Europe and Eurasia
Period of Performance:
September 2026 – March 31st 2027

Scope:
CIPE is seeking a full-time, exempt position based in Washington, D.C. for a Senior Program Manager for Central Asia. This position is responsible for the development and implementation of CIPE’s strategic focus on democratic governance through private sector collective action initiatives to improve business participation, economic freedom, and opportunity across the region by developing regional and country strategies, communications strategies, project implementation, and support grants to local business organizations, think tanks, and chambers of commerce. The position will manage CIPE’s U.S. Department of State-funded Central Asia Migration Entrepreneurship Program (CAMEP) and UK FCDO-funded “Equipping Central Asian Business to Navigate Global Economic Security Issues – Phase II” project.

Responsibilities:

Contribute to the development and implementation of strategy for accomplishing CIPE’s objectives on improving democratic governance and advancing market reforms in region.
Design, implement, and manage a portfolio of projects and grants for the assigned region, supportive of CIPE’s overall goals and strategies for target countries. Project responsibilities have the following dimensions:
Develop project concept papers, proposals, reports, and correspondence.

Lead and contribute to business development efforts by drafting full proposals narratives, technical sections of proposal narratives, budget inputs, or other thematic documents.
Analyze, research, and be familiar with the region’s political and economic landscape, identifying opportunities for CIPE programs and partners.

Collaborate with partners to refine project proposals, monitoring and evaluation plans, and project budgets.
Implement, monitor, and manage all project activities, in collaboration with local partner organizations and CIPE team members.
Establish and maintain regular communication with project partners and other stakeholders.

Develop project reports, summaries, and assessments.

Perform other duties as assigned.

new_jobs.description:
SMBC Group is a top-tier global financial group. Headquartered in Tokyo and with a 400-year history, SMBC Group offers a diverse range of financial services, including banking, leasing, securities, credit cards, and consumer finance. The Group has more than 130 offices and 80,000 employees worldwide in nearly 40 countries. Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group, Inc. (SMFG) is the holding company of SMBC Group, which is one of the three largest banking groups in Japan. SMFG’s shares trade on the Tokyo, Nagoya, and New York (NYSE: SMFG) stock exchanges.

In the Americas, SMBC Group has a presence in the US, Canada, Mexico, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, and Peru. Backed by the capital strength of SMBC Group and the value of its relationships in Asia, the Group offers a range of commercial and investment banking services to its corporate, institutional, and municipal clients. It connects a diverse client base to local markets and the organization’s extensive global network. The Group’s operating companies in the Americas include Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. (SMBC), SMBC Nikko Securities America, Inc., SMBC Capital Markets, Inc., SMBC MANUBANK, JRI America, Inc., SMBC Leasing and Finance, Inc., Banco Sumitomo Mitsui Brasileiro S.A., and Sumitomo Mitsui Finance and Leasing Co., Ltd.

Role Description

SMBC is seeking a highly analytical Analyst to support reporting, metrics, and business intelligence activities within Anti-Fraud Operations Governance Team. This role will be responsible for producing and analyzing fraud management reports, operational dashboards, key risk indicators (KRIs), and executive-level metrics used to monitor fraud trends, operational performance, and fraud losses.

The Analyst will partner with Fraud Operations, Risk Management, Compliance, Technology, and business stakeholders to ensure accurate reporting, identify actionable insights, and support data-driven decision-making across the fraud program.

Responsibilities

Produce and distribute daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly fraud operations reports and dashboards.
Compile, validate, and analyze fraud metrics, fraud losses, alert volumes, investigation outcomes, productivity statistics, and key risk indicators (KRIs).
Develop executive-level reporting packages for senior management, committees, audits, and regulatory examinations.
Monitor reporting accuracy and perform data quality reviews to ensure integrity and consistency of management information.
Identify trends, anomalies, and emerging fraud risks through data analysis and reporting.
Create and maintain dashboards, scorecards, and visualizations using reporting and analytics tools.
Support recurring reporting for governance forums, risk committees, and leadership meetings.
Partner with Technology and data teams to automate reporting processes and improve reporting efficiency.
Assist with regulatory exams, audits, and information requests by gathering, validating, and presenting data.
Track operational performance against established service level agreements (SLAs), KPIs, and departmental objectives.
Maintain reporting procedures, methodologies, and documentation.
Support ad hoc analysis and special projects related to fraud trends, operational effectiveness, and strategic initiatives.

Qualifications And Skills

Bachelor's degree in Business, Finance, Data Analytics, Information Systems, Mathematics, or a related field.
1-3 years of experience in reporting, analytics, operations, risk management, fraud operations, or financial services.
Strong analytical and quantitative skills with the ability to interpret large data sets.
Advanced Microsoft Excel skills, including Pivot Tables, formulas, and data analysis functions.
Experience creating reports, dashboards, and management presentations.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with Power BI, Tableau, SQL, Alteryx, or other reporting and visualization tools.
Knowledge of fraud operations, financial crimes, banking operations, or risk management.
Experience supporting audits, regulatory exams, or governance reporting.
Familiarity with Actimize, Mitek, or other fraud detection platforms.

Additional Requirements

SMBC’s employees participate in a Hybrid workforce model that provides employees with an opportunity to work from home, as well as, from an SMBC office. SMBC requires that employees live within a reasonable commuting distance of their office location. Prospective candidates will learn more about their specific hybrid work schedule during their interview process. Hybrid work may not be permitted for certain roles, including, for example, certain FINRA-registered roles for which in-office attendance for the entire workweek is required.

SMBC provides reasonable accommodations during candidacy for applicants with disabilities consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. If you need a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please let us know at accommodations@smbcgroup.com.
